advisor_description:
A majestic canopy tree developing an expansive, rounded crown with rugged, scaly bark and two-toned lustrous foliage—deep emerald green above and silvery downy-white beneath that shimmer in the breeze. Autumn foliage turns warm bronze to golden-yellow, holding stout sweet acorns prized by wildlife.

Growth Habit & Form: Slow to moderate grower reaching 50–70 ft with an equal or greater spread. Develops a massive root system that adapts far better to heavy, compacted clay and periodic waterlogging than most oaks.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Keystone canopy anchor; forms the architectural overstory for woodland and meadow matrices, shading shade-tolerant sedges and spring ephemerals without surface-root competition.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rain gardens, bioswales, stormwater detention basins, large lawn specimens, and native woodland restoration.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Follow ecological cutback practices to protect native pollinators and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Inspect branches in late winter to early spring; prune only during dormant season (before April 1) to prevent Oak Wilt infection. Clear heavy branch drop.
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide deep watering every 2–3 weeks during the first two summers of establishment; fully self-reliant thereafter.
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave fallen oak leaves in surrounding mulch rings; oak leaf litter shelters hundreds of overwintering butterfly and moth chrysalises.
maintenance_guide.winter: Architectural winter silhouette. Young saplings benefit from trunk wrapping or deer cages to protect tender bark from buck rub.
maintenance_guide.division: Deep taproot and broad root system; do not divide or transplant once established. Plant containerized or ball-and-burlap saplings.
maintenance_guide.sources: Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Sow Wild Natives

advisor_description:
A diminutive, charming glade native producing pairs of petite, hooded violet-blue tubular blossoms with white throats from May to July, followed by tiny helmet-shaped seed capsules. Low square stems feature small, rounded, aromatic green leaves.

Growth Habit & Form: Low, mat-forming perennial 4–8 inches tall spreading gradually by slender underground rhizomes and tuberous rootlets.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Front-of-border groundcover and rockery matrix; companions include blue grama, wild petunia, and Missouri primrose.

Recommended Garden Settings: Limestone glades, dry rocky borders, rock gardens, path edging, and dry sunny hellstrips.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Follow ecological cutback practices to protect native pollinators and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Clear debris lightly in early spring at 50°F+; shoots emerge from small underground tubers.
maintenance_guide.summer: Extremely drought and heat tolerant; thrives in thin, rocky, dry alkaline soils in full sun.
maintenance_guide.fall: Curious helmet-shaped seed capsules split to release seeds; foliage recedes quietly.
maintenance_guide.winter: Dormant tuberous rootlets survive harsh winter freezes in rocky ground.
maintenance_guide.division: Divide small rhizome clusters in early spring or fall.
maintenance_guide.sources: Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Sow Wild Natives

advisor_description:
A dependable, clump-forming native sedge with soft, hair-fringed green leaves and upright, cylindrical seed spikes that emerge greenish-brown in late spring, creating a tidy, flowing textural mound.

Growth Habit & Form: Neat clumping habit 1–2 ft tall and 1–1.5 ft wide with fibrous roots.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Adaptable matrix sedge; pairs well in both sunny wet meadows and dry-to-medium borders.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rain gardens, wet swales, prairie borders, and low-profile native turf replacement.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back to 2 inches in early spring at 50°F+.
maintenance_guide.summer: Handles both wet spring moisture and summer dry spells; highly adaptable to clay.
maintenance_guide.fall: Seed spikes mature and drop nutrient-rich seeds for foraging ground birds.
maintenance_guide.winter: Compact tussock protects root crown through freeze-thaw cycles.
maintenance_guide.division: Divide clumps in spring every 3–5 years.

advisor_description:
A show-stopping, long-blooming groundcover sending out sprawling trailing stems lined with deeply lobed leaves and studded with luminous, chalice-like magenta-purple blossoms with bright white centers from May until frost.

Growth Habit & Form: Trailing, mat-forming perennial 6–9 inches tall spreading 2–3 ft wide from a massive, carrot-like deep woody taproot.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Living mulch and rock wall weaver; weaves beautifully through prairie dropseed, coneflowers, and sideoats grama.

Recommended Garden Settings: Sunny borders, rock gardens, dry retaining wall spillers, curbside hellstrips, and hot parking medians.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Follow ecological cutback practices to protect native pollinators and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Trim back dead winter runners in early spring at 50°F+ as new basal leaves sprout from the crown.
maintenance_guide.summer: Virtually indestructible in drought and intense heat; requires sharp drainage and full sun. Never overwater.
maintenance_guide.fall: Flowers continue until the first hard frost. Deep taproot stores rich carbohydrates for winter.
maintenance_guide.winter: Taproot is completely winter hardy; surface runners die back cleanly.
maintenance_guide.division: Deep woody taproot; do not attempt division. Propagate by seed.

advisor_description:
A delightful native mint bearing dense, pagoda-like tiered whorls of pale blue to lavender two-lipped blossoms speckled with purple, held above downy, aromatic, lance-shaped leaves from May to July.

Growth Habit & Form: Erect, clump-forming perennial 1–2 ft tall and 1 ft wide with non-aggressive, polite fibrous root crowns.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Early-season bumblebee engine; much better behaved and less aggressive than wild bergamot; pairs with coreopsis.

Recommended Garden Settings: Sunny borders, dry-to-medium woodland edges, pollinator gardens, and cottage plantings.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Follow ecological cutback practices to protect native pollinators and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back previous year's stems at 50°F+, leaving 8–12 inches of stubble for solitary bee nesting.
maintenance_guide.summer: Drought tolerant once established; enjoys well-drained loams, rocky soils, and partial to full sun.
maintenance_guide.fall: Tiered dried calyx whorls provide structural architectural interest into autumn and winter.
maintenance_guide.winter: Basal leaf rosette stays semi-evergreen through winter under light leaf litter.
maintenance_guide.division: Divide root clumps every 3–4 years in early spring.
maintenance_guide.sources: Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Sow Wild Natives

advisor_description:
A lovely, shade-tolerant woodland aster producing airy, branching sprays of starry pale blue to lavender blossoms with creamy-yellow centers that turn reddish-purple, blooming profusely from September into November.

Growth Habit & Form: Upright, arching perennial 2–3 ft tall and 1.5–2 ft wide with soft, velvety heart-shaped basal leaves.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Late-season shade matrix nectar source; companions include zigzag goldenrod, elm-leaved goldenrod, and sedges.

Recommended Garden Settings: Shaded woodland edges, dry oak savannas, native shade borders, and naturalized woods.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Follow ecological cutback practices to protect native pollinators and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back old stems at 50°F+, leaving 8–12 inches of standing stubble for stem-nesting bees.
maintenance_guide.summer: Exceptional shade and drought tolerance; thrives under greedy tree roots where other asters fail.
maintenance_guide.fall: Crucial autumn fuel for migrating monarchs, native bees, and late-flying pollinators. Retain fluffy seedheads.
maintenance_guide.winter: Fluffy pappus seedheads feed winter songbirds; stems catch fallen leaves for crown warmth.
maintenance_guide.division: Divide mature crowns in early spring as new basal rosettes appear.
maintenance_guide.sources: Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Sow Wild Natives

advisor_description:
The legendary shortgrass prairie sod-former featuring soft, fine-textured grayish-green curly blades that create a dense, low-growing turf requiring little to no mowing. Turns warm beige-buff in winter dormancy.

Growth Habit & Form: Dense, stoloniferous mat-forming perennial grass growing only 4–8 inches tall, spreading rapidly via surface runners.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Native turf replacement and green carpet matrix; suppresses weeds and creates a living low-profile sod.

Recommended Garden Settings: Low-water lawn alternatives, sunny hellstrips, golf course roughs, and erosion-control slopes.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Follow ecological cutback practices to protect native pollinators and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Mow once in late spring to remove winter thatch. Greens up late in spring when soil warms.
maintenance_guide.summer: Requires full sun and well-drained clay or loam; consumes up to 75% less water than traditional Kentucky bluegrass.
maintenance_guide.fall: Goes dormant after first hard freeze, turning soft golden-tan.
maintenance_guide.winter: Dense turf mat prevents winter soil erosion and weed seed germination.
maintenance_guide.division: Easily spread by plugs or surface runners in late spring.
maintenance_guide.sources: Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Sow Wild Natives

advisor_description:
A stately woodland perennial shrub featuring dramatic wand-like 3–6 ft spires of feathery, fragrant white blossoms that glow in the summer shade above deeply dissected astilbe-like foliage. Creates magnificent candelabra floral displays.

Growth Habit & Form: Forms an imposing, upright arching clump 4–6 ft tall and 2–4 ft wide with a massive fibrous root crown.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Woodland architectural focal point; companions include Christmas fern, wild ginger, and woodland phlox.

Recommended Garden Settings: Deep shade borders, woodland garden backdrops, moist shaded foundations, and historic apothecary plantings.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Follow ecological cutback practices to protect native pollinators and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until 50°F+ before cutting back dried flower stalks. Mulch crown with 2 inches of compost.
maintenance_guide.summer: Requires consistent moisture and shade; foliage will scorch in hot, dry afternoon sun.
maintenance_guide.fall: Leaves turn subtle yellow; architectural dried seed stems persist with rattling bead-like capsules.
maintenance_guide.winter: Stout root crown is fully hardy; keep winter leaf mulch over roots.
maintenance_guide.division: Divide large clumps in early spring as new shoots emerge; slow to establish so divide infrequently.
maintenance_guide.sources: Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Sow Wild Natives

advisor_description:
Celebrated for its jaw-dropping winter spectacle—masses of glossy, brilliant scarlet-red berries densely encrust bare gray twigs from November through February. Modest greenish-white spring blossoms feed native bees before foliage drops.

Growth Habit & Form: Grows 6–10 ft tall and wide with an upright, rounded, multi-stemmed suckering form.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Moisture-loving structural shrub; dioecious (requires one male pollinator within 50 feet of female plants for heavy berry set). Pairs with buttonbush and sedges.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rain gardens, pond margins, low soggy swales, winter viewing borders, and holiday floral cutting gardens.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.spring: Prune in early spring before new growth begins to shape or thin older stems. Avoid heavy pruning which reduces berry count.
maintenance_guide.summer: Thrives in acidic, organic, wet to average soils; tolerates standing water and heavy clay.
maintenance_guide.fall: Leaves turn dark purple before dropping sharply after first hard freeze, revealing the glowing berry stems.
maintenance_guide.winter: Breathtaking winter berry display; branches provide winter sustenance for overwintering bluebirds and robins.
maintenance_guide.division: Separate rooted base suckers in early spring while dormant.
maintenance_guide.sources: Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Sow Wild Natives

advisor_description:
An enchanting dwarf woodland iris producing exquisite, ruffled soft lilac-blue blossoms with prominent crested white and golden-yellow ridges on the falls in April and May, held above tidy fans of sword-like emerald leaves.

Growth Habit & Form: Low, creeping rhizomatous groundcover 4–8 inches tall, spreading rapidly to form dense, weed-choking colonies.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Shade matrix groundcover; interplants under deciduous shrubs with woodland phlox, foamflower, and columbine.

Recommended Garden Settings: Shaded rock gardens, moist woodland paths, north-facing slopes, and shaded foundation edges.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.spring: Blossoms open early in spring; avoid burying shallow surface rhizomes under thick heavy mulch.
maintenance_guide.summer: Prefers rich, moist, organic, well-drained soils in partial to full shade; drought tolerant once rooted.
maintenance_guide.fall: Foliage declines cleanly in autumn; rhizomes form a dense network across the soil surface.
maintenance_guide.winter: Surface rhizomes are hardy; a light dusting of fallen leaves provides ideal natural mulch.
maintenance_guide.division: Divide surface rhizomes immediately after spring flowering finishes every 3–4 years.
maintenance_guide.sources: Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Sow Wild Natives

advisor_description:
Unmatched in visual brilliance, shooting up 2–4 ft spikes of blazing velvety scarlet-red tubular blossoms from July to September that act as the premier beacon for migrating Ruby-throated Hummingbirds.

Growth Habit & Form: Erect, unbranched stems 2–4 ft tall forming basal winter rosettes; thrives in wet, rich soils.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Hummingbird magnet; interplant in moist matrices with blue flag iris, great blue lobelia, and carex.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rain gardens, stream margins, wet meadows, retention pond edges, and hummingbird borders.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping or occasional division) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.
maintenance_guide.spring: Do not smother basal green rosettes with heavy mulch in spring; clear leaves so rosettes receive early light.
maintenance_guide.summer: Requires consistent moisture; do not allow roots to dry out. Self-seeds gently in moist bare soil.
maintenance_guide.fall: Allow seed capsules to mature and drop seed naturally. Basal rosette stays evergreen through winter.
maintenance_guide.winter: Evergreen basal rosettes photosynthesize during mild winter days; avoid burying under thick matted leaves.
maintenance_guide.division: Short-lived perennial that renews by offsets; separate and transplant basal plantlets every 2–3 years in spring.
maintenance_guide.sources: Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Sow Wild Natives

advisor_description:
An imposing architectural woodland giant growing like a shrub with massive tri-pinnate leaves up to 3 ft wide, topped in summer with ethereal 12-inch panicles of creamy-green starry flowers, followed by weeping clusters of rich reddish-purple berries.

Growth Habit & Form: Rapidly forms an immense herbaceous shrub 3–5 ft tall and wide each summer, dying back completely to the ground in winter.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Bold tropical-looking shade accent; pairs with wild hydrangeas, ostrich ferns, and black cohosh.

Recommended Garden Settings: Woodland clearings, shady property borders, moist ravine slopes, and large shade gardens.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Follow ecological cutback practices to protect native pollinators and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until 50°F+ before cutting back dead hollow canes. Shoots emerge robustly in late spring.
maintenance_guide.summer: Prefers fertile, humus-rich, moist soils in partial to full shade. Very low pest pressure.
maintenance_guide.fall: Dark purple-black berries are ravenously consumed by wood thrushes, robins, and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.winter: Hollow dried winter canes provide nesting tubes for solitary bees; dies back cleanly to ground.
maintenance_guide.division: Massive aromatic root crown; propagate from fresh seed or divide root crown in early spring.
maintenance_guide.sources: Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Sow Wild Natives

advisor_description:
A rare, majestic native milkweed bearing dense, rounded umbels of deeply saturated, royal magenta-purple to violet star-shaped blossoms in June that glow with extraordinary chromatic richness above broad, velvety deep green leaves.

Growth Habit & Form: Stout, upright unbranched perennial 2–3 ft tall and 1–1.5 ft wide with deep, non-aggressive taproots.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Polite monarch host; unlike common milkweed, it forms a well-behaved clump without aggressive spreading runners.

Recommended Garden Settings: Woodland edge borders, sunny meadows, shaded pollinator gardens, and native show gardens.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.spring: Emerges late in spring (May); mark planting spot. Wait for 50°F+ before clearing old stalks.
maintenance_guide.summer: High-priority monarch butterfly host and nectar plant; thrives in partial shade to full sun.
maintenance_guide.fall: Warty seed pods split to reveal silky parachuting seeds; leave pods to mature naturally.
maintenance_guide.winter: Deep taproot is completely hardy; stems die back cleanly to ground level.
maintenance_guide.division: Deep taproot; do not divide or transplant once established. Grow from fresh seed.

advisor_description:
An enchanting prairie wildflower (cataloged under fern) featuring delicate, fern-like pinnate foliage topped in spring with nodding, reddish-pink bell flowers, followed by sensational, feathery, smoke-like pink seed plumes that glow in backlighting like puffs of pink smoke.

Growth Habit & Form: Low, mat-forming rosette 6–12 inches tall (in fruit) and 8–12 inches wide with creeping rhizomes.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Front-of-border groundcover; companions include blue grama, prairie dropseed, and Missouri primrose.

Recommended Garden Settings: Sunny rock gardens, limestone glades, curbside hellstrips, and prairie border edges.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.spring: Trim tattered winter foliage in early spring at 50°F+ as new fern-like leaves emerge.
maintenance_guide.summer: Requires full sun and sharp, well-drained gravelly or sandy soils; completely intolerant of soggy wet clay.
maintenance_guide.fall: Ferny foliage turns attractive shades of red and purple in autumn.
maintenance_guide.winter: Semi-evergreen rosette stays close to the ground, enduring sub-zero prairie cold.
maintenance_guide.division: Divide creeping rhizomes in early spring or fall.

advisor_description:
A beloved shade shrub bearing massive, domed corymbs of creamy-white florets up to 8 inches across from June into August, fading gracefully to antique papery lime-green and parchment-tan in autumn.

Growth Habit & Form: Forms an arching, rounded mound 3–5 ft tall and wide with broad, serrated bright green foliage.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Understory shrub layer; combines elegantly with wild columbine, ferns, and woodland phlox.

Recommended Garden Settings: North and east building foundations, shaded shrub borders, woodland edges, and cottage gardens.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back stems to 6–12 inches above the ground in early spring (at 50°F+). Blooms reliably on new season wood.
maintenance_guide.summer: Requires partial to full shade and consistent moisture; leaves will droop during midday heat in full sun.
maintenance_guide.fall: Retain dried flower heads on the shrub for decorative fall texture and winter architecture.
maintenance_guide.winter: Dried parchment-colored flower globes catch drifting snow and shelter beneficial insects.

advisor_description:
A breathtaking understory gem bearing erect 6–10 inch panicles of fiery tubular red flowers in mid-spring, precisely timed with the arrival of migrating Ruby-throated Hummingbirds. Features lustrous, dark green palmate leaves followed by smooth light brown buckeye nuts.

Growth Habit & Form: Grows 12–15 ft tall and wide as a multi-stemmed large shrub or compact small tree with a handsome rounded canopy.

Sociability & Matrix Role: High-impact seasonal nectar engine; combines exquisitely with eastern redbud, wild columbine, and woodland phlox.

Recommended Garden Settings: Hummingbird gardens, shaded foundation borders, woodland openings, and rain garden perimeters.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.spring: Apply a 2-inch compost mulch layer in early spring. Remove any dead or broken branches after flowering.
maintenance_guide.summer: Foliage may naturally drop early in August during prolonged hot, dry spells without harming the tree's health; provide supplemental water to prolong foliage retention.
maintenance_guide.fall: Buckeye seeds drop in early autumn; poisonous to humans and pets, but eagerly buried by squirrels.
maintenance_guide.winter: Stout winter buds with prominent triangular leaf scars add subtle architectural character.

advisor_description:
An elegant, fragrant wetland milkweed topped from July to August with abundant, sweet-scented umbels of soft rose-pink to mauve-magenta blossoms smelling intensely of vanilla and cinnamon, attracting legions of swallowtails and monarchs.

Growth Habit & Form: Upright, branched perennial 3–5 ft tall and 2–3 ft wide with a deep, non-invasive fibrous root clump.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Premier monarch host for moist gardens; well-behaved clump habit; pairs with swamp sunflower, blue flag iris, and sedges.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rain gardens, bioswales, pond shorelines, wet meadows, and irrigated perennial borders.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summer: Requires consistent moisture; thrives in heavy clay and standing water, but adapts well to average garden soil.

maintenance_guide.winter: Stout woody stems stand erect through winter winds and snow.

advisor_description:
A charming iris-family native featuring flat, grass-like foliage topped in late spring with starry, violet-blue blossoms with bright golden-yellow centers that open in sunshine and close on cloudy days.

Growth Habit & Form: Clump-forming perennial 8–12 inches tall and 6–10 inches wide with fibrous roots.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Front-of-border accent and matrix filler; companions include prairie alumroot, wild petunia, and sedges.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rock gardens, cottage borders, path edges, rain garden margins, and low-profile meadows.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.spring: Clear fallen leaves from crowns in early spring; trim dead tips as green shoots emerge.
maintenance_guide.summer: Prefers moist to average, well-drained soils in full sun to light shade; avoid dry baking heat.
maintenance_guide.fall: Small spherical seed capsules ripen in summer and fall.
maintenance_guide.winter: Semi-evergreen in mild winters; keep crown protected with light leaf litter.

advisor_description:
A refined, bushy woodland native producing loose, airy sprays of delicate, 5-petaled star-like white blossoms with reddish calyxes in late spring that float like dancing butterflies above deeply incised, textured trifoliate foliage. Turns brilliant copper and peach in fall.

Growth Habit & Form: Forms a dense, multi-stemmed, shrub-like mound 2–3 ft tall and wide with a woody rootstock.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Structural shade matrix perennial; pairs with woodland phlox, wild geranium, and maidenhair fern.

Recommended Garden Settings: Woodland edge borders, dry shade, native cottage plantings, and dappled foundation borders.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

advisor_description:
A spectacular, non-invasive native honeysuckle producing profuse, tubular coral-red blossoms with golden-yellow interiors from May through September, followed by clusters of bright red berries. The premier native nectar vine for Ruby-throated Hummingbirds.

Growth Habit & Form: Twining, semi-evergreen woody vine climbing 10–20 ft by twining stems without invasive aerial rootlets.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Vertical hummingbird magnet; safe for arbors and fences, never choking mature trees like invasive Asian honeysuckles.

Recommended Garden Settings: Trellises, arbors, patio pergolas, chain-link fence screening, and mailbox posts.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summer: Enjoys moist, rich, well-drained loams in full sun for heaviest flowering; highly mildew resistant.
maintenance_guide.fall: Bright red berries in autumn feed purple finches, goldfinches, and hermit thrushes.
maintenance_guide.winter: Semi-evergreen blue-green foliage persists into winter; woody twining stems are very hardy.

advisor_description:
A magnificent 4-season powerhouse opening in spring with profuse corymbs of 5-petaled white flowers with pink anthers, followed by glossy dark green summer leaves, clusters of antioxidant-rich glossy black chokeberries in August, and blazing wine-red fall foliage.

Growth Habit & Form: Grows 3–6 ft tall and wide with an upright, spreading, multi-stemmed habit, suckering gradually into a tidy colony.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Adaptable matrix shrub; pairs with little bluestem, ninebark, and black-eyed susans in wet or dry soils.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rain gardens, edible homestead plantings, erosion control banks, and foundation shrub borders.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summer: Highly pest and disease free; tolerant of both boggy standing water and summer drought.
maintenance_guide.fall: Vivid crimson autumn color rivals burning bush. Edible tart berries make nutrient-dense syrups and jams.
maintenance_guide.winter: Dark smooth twigs hold persistent berries that feed cedar waxwings in late winter.

advisor_description:
A succulent botanical gem producing clusters of cylindrical, fleshy green leaves topped on wiry 8–12 inch stems with glowing, 1-inch vivid magenta-rose blossoms with golden stamens that open exclusively in afternoon sunshine for just a few hours.

Growth Habit & Form: Low, succulent rosette 8–12 inches tall (in bloom) and 6 inches wide with a fleshy, drought-storing root.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Glade and rockery specialist; companions include Missouri primrose, blue grama, and wild petunia.

Recommended Garden Settings: Sandstone and limestone glades, gravel gardens, sunny trough containers, rock crevices, and hellstrips.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

A sturdy wetland perennial bearing curious, hooded rose-pink snapdragon-like blossoms resembling the open beaks of turtles from August to October, set against handsome, coarsely serrated dark green lustrous foliage.

Growth Habit & Form: Upright, sturdy clump 2–3 ft tall and 1.5–2 ft wide that spreads slowly via short underground rhizomes.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Late-season moisture matrix perennial; companions include cardinal flower, great blue lobelia, and buttonbush.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rain gardens, stream margins, wet shady borders, retention pond edges, and bioswales.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

A tough, ornamental native shrub featuring peeling papery bark in distinctive shredded layers, dense button-like clusters of pink-tinted white flowers in late spring, papery red seed capsules, and attractive lobed leaves turning bronze-purple in fall.

Growth Habit & Form: Upright, arching shrub 6–10 ft tall and wide with a vigorous, fountain-like spreading silhouette.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Structural hedgerow shrub; provides dense nesting cover and pairs well with goldenrods and big bluestem.

Recommended Garden Settings: Stream bank stabilization, screening hedges, rocky glade borders, and low-maintenance slopes.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

Growth Habit & Form: Slender, vertical spire 1.5–2.5 ft tall and 1 ft wide arising from a hard, rounded, drought-proof underground corm.

Sociability & Matrix Role: High-impact pollinator magnet; pairs with sideoats grama, Missouri primrose, and glade coneflower.

Recommended Garden Settings: Dry rocky glades, sunny borders, limestone outcroppings, rock gardens, and curbside hellstrips.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

Growth Habit & Form: Forms a tidy, non-spreading clumping mound 6–12 inches tall and 12–18 inches wide.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Well-behaved shade clumper; companions include wild columbine, wild ginger, and alumroot.

Recommended Garden Settings: Dry woodland slopes, shaded rock gardens, path edging, and contemplative shade borders.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.sources: Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Sow Wild Natives

advisor_description:
A luminous woodland aster erupting in September and October with frothy clouds of starry, pale blue to lavender blossoms with yellow centers that mature to reddish-purple. Features distinctive heart-shaped basal leaves.

Growth Habit & Form: Forms a bushy, multi-branched mound 2–3 ft tall and 2 ft wide, filling the autumn woodland canopy with color.

Sociability & Matrix Role: High-capacity late-season pollinator lifeline; companions include zigzag goldenrod and woodland phlox.

Recommended Garden Settings: Woodland edge borders, dry-to-moist shade gardens, cottage borders, and shaded pollinator beds.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Follow ecological cutback practices to protect native pollinators and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back previous year's stems at 50°F+, leaving 8–12 inches of stubble for stem-nesting native bees.
maintenance_guide.summer: Very drought and shade tolerant once established; pinch stem tips in June for bushier habit.
maintenance_guide.fall: Spectacular autumn flower cloud buzzes with late native bees and migrating monarchs. Leave seedheads.
maintenance_guide.winter: Fluffy seedheads feed winter songbirds; dried stems protect dormant crown.
maintenance_guide.division: Divide root clumps every 3–4 years in spring to maintain vigor and control spread.
maintenance_guide.sources: Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Sow Wild Natives

advisor_description:
A beloved evergreen Missouri native fern featuring thick, leathery, deep emerald-green pinnate fronds with stocking-shaped pinnae resembling Christmas stockings. The fertile upper tips bear rusty sori and wither, leaving lustrous dark green sterile fronds all winter.

Growth Habit & Form: Forms a vase-shaped, arching evergreen clump 1–2 ft tall and 1.5–2 ft wide with a fibrous, non-spreading root crown.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Evergreen shade matrix anchor; companions include wild ginger, woodland phlox, and columbine.

Recommended Garden Settings: Shaded slopes, north-facing foundations, woodland shade gardens, rock gardens, and winter borders.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Follow ecological cutback practices to protect native pollinators and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Leave old evergreen fronds intact all winter to protect the crown; gently snip off tattered fronds in April as silvery, fuzzy fiddleheads uncurl.
maintenance_guide.summer: Highly drought-tolerant once established; thrives in rocky, well-drained acidic to neutral woodland soil in deep shade.
maintenance_guide.fall: Fronds remain deep, glossy green as deciduous canopy leaves drop.
maintenance_guide.winter: Lies prostrate against the earth in winter, holding fallen leaves to protect roots and preventing hillside erosion.
maintenance_guide.division: Clump former; rarely needs division. Divide large multi-crowned clumps in early spring.

advisor_description:
An architectural marvel featuring tall, fountain-like stems clothed in thousands of drooping, weeping, willow-like linear leaves that resemble cascading botanical fountains all summer, exploding in October with sprays of golden-yellow daisies.

Growth Habit & Form: Towering, clumping perennial 5–8 ft tall and 3–4 ft wide with a bold, weeping structural presence.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Structural accent; back-of-border architectural giant; companions include big bluestem, switchgrass, and ironweed.

Recommended Garden Settings: Limestone glade borders, large meadow restorations, sunny boundary screening, and architectural focal points.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping or occasional division) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back previous year's dead stalks at 50°F+. Pinch or cut stems back by half in early June to reduce height and encourage bushier flowering.
maintenance_guide.summer: Very drought and rocky soil tolerant; handles shallow limestone with ease. May need staking if soil is too rich.
maintenance_guide.fall: Magnificent late-season bloom cloud feeds migrating monarchs and native bees. Prolific seed crop for birds.
maintenance_guide.winter: Stout dried stems provide strong winter architecture.
maintenance_guide.division: Divide large crowns in spring every 3–4 years.
maintenance_guide.sources: Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Sow Wild Natives

advisor_description:
A magnificent tallgrass prairie monarch forming a stately, columnar blue-green vase topped in late summer with immense, airy, pink-tinged cloud-like flower panicles that look like botanical fireworks. Foliage turns glowing bright yellow and bronze in fall.

Growth Habit & Form: Stout, upright clumping grass 4–6 ft tall and 2–3 ft wide with a deep, tenacious root system reaching 10 ft into the earth.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Structural matrix grass; provides vertical architecture behind coneflowers, asters, and goldenrods.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rain gardens, bioswales, sunny screening hedges, prairie restorations, and winter focal points.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Follow ecological cutback practices to protect native pollinators and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back to 3–4 inches in late spring at 50°F+. Leaves emerging in May.
maintenance_guide.summer: Adaptable to almost any soil from sand to wet heavy clay; drought and flood tolerant.
maintenance_guide.fall: Vivid golden-yellow fall color; heavy seed panicles feed game birds, songbirds, and finches.
maintenance_guide.winter: Unbeatable winter architecture; stiff columnar stems stand proud through heavy snowdrifts.
maintenance_guide.division: Divide large dormant crowns in early spring with a sharp spade every 5–8 years.
maintenance_guide.sources: Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Sow Wild Natives

advisor_description:
A colossal prairie giant producing immense, leathery, sandpaper-textured spade-shaped basal leaves up to 2 ft long that smell resinously of cedar and turpentine, sending up smooth, leafless 6–9 ft wands topped with bright yellow sunflower heads in late summer.

Growth Habit & Form: Massive basal rosette sending up vertical stalks 6–9 ft tall from a massive, deep taproot penetrating 10–15 feet into the prairie subsoil.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Prairie keystone monarch; pairs with compass plant, big bluestem, and cup plant in open sun.

Recommended Garden Settings: Prairie restorations, large sunny borders, acreage meadows, and native educational gardens.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until 50°F+ before cutting back dried flower stalks. Basal leaves emerge robustly in May.
maintenance_guide.summer: Completely drought-proof once taproot is established; defies the most brutal Midwestern heatwaves.
maintenance_guide.fall: Large flat seeds are eagerly harvested by American Goldfinches; leave stalks standing.
maintenance_guide.winter: Stout, woody wands stand like architectural sentinels against winter blizzards.
maintenance_guide.division: Massive woody taproot; impossible to divide once established. Plant containerized saplings or seeds.

advisor_description:
A neat, tufted woodland sedge with glossy, dark green narrow leaves that creates a refined, grassy accent in rich forest soils, blooming in spring with distinctive small spikes featuring long, leaf-like bracts.

Growth Habit & Form: Compact, tidy clump 6–10 inches tall and wide with a non-invasive, polite habit.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Solitary woodland clumper; interplants elegantly with woodland phlox, bellwort, and trillium.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rich deciduous woodlands, shaded borders, native rain garden margins, and shaded path borders.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.spring: Trim back dead leaf tips in early spring as new bright green blades emerge.
maintenance_guide.summer: Prefers rich, moist, organic loams in partial to full shade.
maintenance_guide.fall: Dark green color persists late into autumn.
maintenance_guide.winter: Evergreen to semi-evergreen crown survives cold Midwest winters.
maintenance_guide.division: Divide clumps in spring as new growth starts.

advisor_description:
A dazzling, profusely blooming annual/short-lived perennial native producing masses of vibrant bi-colored daisy blossoms—bright golden-yellow petals with rich mahogany-maroon centers—fluttering on slender, airy stems from June until frost.

Growth Habit & Form: Upright, airy, multi-branched mound 1.5–3 ft tall and 1–1.5 ft wide with fine, ferny foliage.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Prolific seasonal filler; quickly colonizes bare spots in meadows, companioning with little bluestem and black-eyed susans.

Recommended Garden Settings: Pollinator meadows, quick wildflower covers, rain garden edges, cottage beds, and cut-flower gardens.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.spring: Seeds germinate readily in warming spring soil; thin seedlings to 6–10 inches apart.
maintenance_guide.summer: Blooms continuously in full sun; shearing spent flowers midsummer stimulates a fresh autumn bloom flush.
maintenance_guide.fall: Allow late flowers to set seed; self-sows reliably year after year without becoming invasive.
maintenance_guide.winter: Plants die after frost; seeds overwinter in soil.
maintenance_guide.division: Annual; easily propagated by broadcasting seed in spring or autumn.

advisor_description:
A regal wetland wildflower sending up stiff, square stems crowned in mid-to-late summer with candelabra-like branched spikes of rich violet-blue to purple florets that open progressively from bottom to top, surrounded by serrated lance-shaped leaves.

Growth Habit & Form: Erect, columnar clump 3–5 ft tall and 1.5–2 ft wide with fibrous, non-aggressive roots.

Sociability & Matrix Role: High-volume pollinator magnet; pairs with swamp milkweed, Joe-Pye weed, and blue flag iris.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rain gardens, bioswales, retention pond margins, wet meadows, and sunny drainage ditches.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back dried stems at 50°F+, leaving 12–18 inches of stubble for solitary bee nesting.
maintenance_guide.summer: Thrives in wet to medium-moist soils in full sun; tolerates brief dry spells once established.
maintenance_guide.fall: Candelabra seed heads mature to dark brown; seeds feed cardinals, juncos, and native sparrows.
maintenance_guide.winter: Distinctive candelabra silhouettes provide handsome vertical winter structure.
maintenance_guide.division: Divide root clumps every 3 years in spring; self-sows gently in moist soils.

advisor_description:
A magnificent, shrub-like native legume producing lush, tropical-looking pinnate foliage topped in July and August with showy axillary clusters of bright golden-yellow blossoms with contrasting dark brown anthers, followed by flat black seed pods.

Growth Habit & Form: Forms a dense, robust, multi-stemmed shrub-like clump 3–5 ft tall and 2–3 ft wide.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Primary larval host plant for Cloudless Sulphur and Sleepy Orange butterflies; pairs with prairie grasses.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rain gardens, prairie meadows, back-of-border plantings, and butterfly breeding sanctuaries.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Follow ecological cutback practices to protect native pollinators and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut woody-stemmed canes back to 6 inches in early spring (at 50°F+). Shoots emerge late in May.
maintenance_guide.summer: Highly drought and heat tolerant once established; enjoys full sun to partial shade and adapts to heavy clay.
maintenance_guide.fall: Flat brown seed pods persist and rattle in autumn; seeds provide high-protein winter food for Northern Bobwhite quail.
maintenance_guide.winter: Woody canes stand erect through winter; root system is completely cold hardy.
maintenance_guide.division: Deep woody root system; best propagated by seed treated with boiling water scarification.

advisor_description:
A beloved woodland spring jewel producing large, 2-inch glossy bright buttercup-yellow blossoms with bushy golden stamens in April and May, held above deeply lobed, blue-green oak-like foliage. Stems emit a yellow sap when bruised.

Growth Habit & Form: Forms a lush, mounding clump 12–18 inches tall and wide with fleshy rootstocks.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Woodland spring matrix star; pairs with Virginia bluebells, columbine, wild ginger, and ferns.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rich woodland shade gardens, shaded borders, north-facing slopes, and naturalized shade carpets.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.spring: Allow blossoms to open freely; foliage provides magnificent weed-smothering groundcover.
maintenance_guide.summer: Requires partial to full shade and rich, moist, organic soils; may go dormant in extreme summer heat and drought.
maintenance_guide.fall: Nodding, bristly green seed pods split to drop seeds; readily self-seeds to form delightful colonies.
maintenance_guide.winter: Dormant crowns survive deep winter freezes under a natural blanket of fallen leaves.
maintenance_guide.division: Divide dormant clumps in late summer or early spring.

advisor_description:
A vital wildlife understory tree producing dense 3–6 inch cylindrical racemes of fragrant white flowers in late spring, giving way to hanging clusters of tart, deep purple-black cherries in late summer that sparkle against vibrant autumn yellow foliage.

Growth Habit & Form: Forms an upright, arching multi-stem small tree or large shrub 20–30 ft tall and 15–20 ft wide, suckering to create dense defensive wildlife thickets.

Sociability & Matrix Role: High-value keystone species supporting hundreds of lepidoptera caterpillars; sociable thicket-former ideal for habitat borders.

Recommended Garden Settings: Wildlife windbreaks, woodland edges, hedgerows, and soil stabilization slopes.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping or occasional division) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.
maintenance_guide.spring: Remove root suckers annually if a tidy single-stem or small cluster tree is preferred. Inspect for black knot gall and excise infected stems 4 inches below gall.
maintenance_guide.summer: Very drought tolerant once established; cherries ripen from red to deep purple-black in August.
maintenance_guide.fall: Fruit is eagerly stripped by thrushes, catbirds, and grosbeaks. Fallen foliage feeds beneficial detritivores.
maintenance_guide.winter: Provide rabbit wire guards around young trunks during harsh winters.
maintenance_guide.division: Suckers can be severed in late winter; propagate by stratified seed.

advisor_description:
An exceptionally robust, heat- and humidity-tolerant alumroot producing massive, velvety maple-like scalloped leaves covered in fine hairs, topped in late summer and autumn (August–October) with airy 2–3 ft panicles of tiny creamy-white starry blossoms.

Growth Habit & Form: Dense, mounding semi-evergreen clump 12–18 inches tall (foliage) and 2–3 ft tall in bloom, spreading 18–24 inches wide.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Late-blooming shade matrix workhorse; companions include Japanese painted fern, wild ginger, and carex.

Recommended Garden Settings: Shaded rock gardens, foundation borders, shaded retaining wall crevices, and autumn borders.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until 50°F+ before trimming tattered winter foliage; new velvety leaves emerge from the central woody crown.
maintenance_guide.summer: Extremely heat, humidity, and drought tolerant compared to hybrid heucheras; thrives in rocky, well-drained soils.
maintenance_guide.fall: Spectacular late-season floral haze feeds late-season native bees and butterflies.
maintenance_guide.winter: Velvety foliage is evergreen in mild winters; mulch lightly to prevent freeze-thaw frost heaving.

advisor_description:
The largest-flowered native penstemon, bearing magnificent 2-inch bell-shaped blossoms of pale lavender, pink, or white marked with intricate purple nectar guides in May and June, set on stout stems with thick, glossy, tooth-edged leaves.

Growth Habit & Form: Upright, sturdy clump 1.5–2 ft tall and 1 ft wide with a fibrous, drought-hardy root crown.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Glade and border showstopper; prime bumblebee flower; pairs with sideoats grama, Missouri primrose, and glade coneflower.

Recommended Garden Settings: Limestone glades, dry sunny borders, rock gardens, curbside hellstrips, and low-water plantings.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summer: Requires full sun and sharply drained, alkaline rocky or gravelly soil; completely intolerant of soggy wet clay.
maintenance_guide.fall: Woody, pointed seed capsules ripen; seeds feed native birds.
maintenance_guide.winter: Semi-evergreen basal rosette hugs the ground, withstanding sub-zero temperatures.
maintenance_guide.division: Short-lived perennial that self-sows politely; divide crowns in spring.

advisor_description:
An exceptionally versatile, sun-loving sedge forming cheerful fountains of medium-green foliage topped in late spring with dense, rounded green-to-copper oval seed spikes resembling tiny pinecones.

Growth Habit & Form: Tussock-forming clumping habit 1–2 ft tall and 1.5 ft wide with deep, fibrous roots.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Sun-to-shade matrix sedge; companions include purple coneflower, butterfly weed, and blue-eyed grass.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rain gardens, bioswales, sunny meadows, prairie borders, and stormwater basins.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summer: Tolerates wet clay in spring and baking drought in summer; extremely resilient native sedge.
maintenance_guide.fall: Seed spikes turn golden-bronze and drop seeds that feed songbirds.
maintenance_guide.winter: Dried tufts hold their rounded form throughout winter.
maintenance_guide.division: Easily divided in spring.

advisor_description:
Sweetly spicy clove-scented golden-yellow trumpet blossoms cover arching branches in April, followed by lobed maple-like leaves, edible sweet black currants in July, and rich reddish-purple fall color.

Growth Habit & Form: Grows 6–8 ft tall and wide with an arching, vase-shaped form that spreads by rhizomatous root suckers.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Nectar magnet for early-season queen bumblebees and hummingbirds; pairs with prairie dropseed and coneflowers.

Recommended Garden Settings: Edible native gardens, fragrant shrub borders, sunny slopes, and woodland transitions.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

advisor_description:
An extraordinary botanical wonder blooming in late autumn (October–December) with spidery, fragrant ribbon-like yellow petals along bare branches, while foliage turns vivid golden-yellow. Emits a clean, woodsy perfume in the crisp fall air.

Growth Habit & Form: Multi-stemmed large shrub or small understory tree 15–20 ft tall and wide with an irregular, picturesque vase silhouette.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Woodland edge structural element; provides critical late-season nectar for late-flying owlet moths and winter pollinators.

Recommended Garden Settings: Woodland margins, north/east building exposures, rain garden perimeters, and naturalized bird borders.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summer: Prefers consistently moist, organically rich, acidic to neutral soils; mulch well to keep roots cool.

advisor_description:
A fast-growing red oak relative featuring glossy, deeply lobed dark green foliage that blazes with brilliant scarlet and deep red autumn color, persisting late into November. Forms a handsome pyramidal crown maturing to rounded fullness.

Growth Habit & Form: Reaches 40–60 ft with a 35–45 ft spread. Possesses strong structural branching and superior tolerance to bottomland flooding, alkaline clay soils, and urban compaction.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Dominant canopy tree; casts moderate shade that pairs well with understory dogwoods, spicebush, and forest sedges.

Recommended Garden Settings: Street tree lawns, urban residential yards, wet floodplain edges, and prairie transition groves.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Follow ecological cutback practices to protect native pollinators and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Perform any structural pruning in January or February while fully dormant to prevent oak bark beetle transmission.
maintenance_guide.summer: Water deeply during severe drought in first 2 years; exceptional heat and wet-soil resilience once established.
maintenance_guide.fall: Enjoy long-lasting scarlet autumn foliage. Allow leaf litter to decompose under canopy to nourish soil mycelium.
maintenance_guide.winter: Stout branches resist ice storm damage. Protect trunk base from winter rodent gnawing.
maintenance_guide.division: Deep root network; plant young trees in permanent location; never transplant mature specimens.

advisor_description:
An electric, long-blooming native verbena creating vibrant carpets of rich rose-pink to magenta tubular blossom clusters from April through October above dark green, deeply lobed creeping foliage.

Growth Habit & Form: Sprawling, trailing perennial 6–12 inches tall and 18–24 inches wide with stems that root at leaf nodes.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Front-of-border groundcover and rockery matrix; pairs with prairie dropseed, blue grama, and wild petunia.

Recommended Garden Settings: Sunny rock gardens, retaining wall spillers, curbside hellstrips, glade gardens, and border fronts.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.spring: Trim back tattered winter stems in early spring (50°F+) to stimulate fresh branching.
maintenance_guide.summer: Thrives in full sun, intense heat, and well-drained rocky or sandy soils; shear spent blooms for continuous flowering.
maintenance_guide.fall: Flowers continue persistently until the first hard autumn freeze.
maintenance_guide.winter: Semi-evergreen in mild winters; needs well-drained soil to prevent crown rot during winter wet.
maintenance_guide.division: Rooted runners can be severed and transplanted in spring.

advisor_description:
The common, adaptable woodland sedge producing lustrous, broad blue-green leaves and abundant creamy-white spring flower spikes, forming a handsome, relaxed fountain of foliage.

Growth Habit & Form: Grows 1–2 ft tall and wide, clumping and self-seeding readily to colonize disturbed shade soils.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Robust colonizer; fills bare spots under trees and along shady paths where lawn grass fails.

Recommended Garden Settings: Woodland restoration, dry-to-moist shade, shaded utility easements, and bank cover.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.fall: Provides continuous green cover through autumn.
maintenance_guide.winter: Semi-evergreen foliage persists through snow.

advisor_description:
The crowning monarch of autumn native asters, exploding in September and October with profuse, 1.5-inch daisy blossoms of vivid royal purple to deep magenta with glowing golden centers, borne on robust, hairy stems with aromatic clasping leaves.

Growth Habit & Form: Upright, vase-shaped clump 3–5 ft tall and 2–3 ft wide with a fibrous, sturdy root crown.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Crucial late-season monarch fueling station; companions include showy goldenrod, little bluestem, and switchgrass.

Recommended Garden Settings: Sunny perennial borders, prairie restorations, rain garden edges, and pollinator meadows.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping or occasional division) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back previous year's dead stalks at 50°F+, leaving 12 inches of stubble for solitary bee nesting.
maintenance_guide.summer: Apply a 'Chelsea chop' in late May or early June by cutting stems back by one-third to half to induce branching, reduce height, and prevent flopping. Needs consistent moisture.
maintenance_guide.fall: Breathtaking autumn bloom clouds buzz with bumblebees and migrating monarchs. Retain seedheads.
maintenance_guide.winter: Fluffy seedheads feed winter goldfinches; basal rosette overwinters green.
maintenance_guide.division: Divide root clumps every 3 years in early spring to maintain vigor and center fullness.
maintenance_guide.sources: Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Sow Wild Natives

advisor_description:
Known as Fox Sedge for its distinctive, bushy, bristly seed heads in late spring that resemble a fluffy fox's tail. Forms dense, handsome fountains of narrow bright green foliage.

Growth Habit & Form: Tussock-forming bunch sedge 2–3 ft tall and 1.5–2 ft wide with robust fibrous roots.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Wetland matrix workhorse; combines with swamp milkweed, blue flag iris, and soft rush.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rain gardens, bioswales, retention pond margins, wet drainage ditches, and stream banks.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

A whimsical prairie perennial bearing nodding, crook-necked umbels of soft pink to lilac bell-shaped blossoms in midsummer that dangle gracefully above flat, narrow, onion-scented blue-green foliage.

Growth Habit & Form: Clumping bulbous perennial 12–18 inches tall and 8–12 inches wide, multiplying into handsome clumps.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Pollinator magnet; completely deer- and rabbit-resistant due to allicin scent; pairs with prairie dropseed and coneflowers.

Recommended Garden Settings: Pollinator borders, rock gardens, cottage borders, hellstrips, and herb gardens.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

Growth Habit & Form: Compact, fine-textured clumping grass 9–15 inches tall and wide with dense fibrous roots.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Low-growing matrix groundcover; companion to prairie smoke, wild petunia, and Missouri primrose.

Recommended Garden Settings: Curbside hellstrips, green roofs, rock gardens, low-mow native lawns, and front-of-border edges.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

An exquisite native woodland groundcover forming an unbroken, weed-smothering carpet of velvety, heart-shaped to kidney-shaped deep emerald leaves up to 6 inches wide. In early spring, curious 3-petaled maroon-brown jug-like flowers hide beneath the foliage.

Growth Habit & Form: Low, creeping rhizomatous groundcover 4–8 inches tall, spreading steadily via shallow, aromatic underground rhizomes.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Premier shade matrix groundcover; completely suppresses weeds under trees alongside ferns and woodland phlox.

Recommended Garden Settings: Deep shade woodland gardens, north foundation beds, tree-root shade carpets, and shaded ravine slopes.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

An architectural, long-lived prairie native producing flat-topped, cauliflower-like corymbs of pearly-white, woolly button blossoms from June to August, held proudly above large, leathery, scabrous dark green foliage that resembles horse-radish.

Growth Habit & Form: Stout, upright clump 2–4 ft tall and 1.5–2 ft wide with an exceptionally deep, drought-proof woody taproot.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Textural contrast matrix perennial; pairs with purple coneflower, butterfly weed, and prairie dropseed.

Recommended Garden Settings: Sunny perennial borders, prairie restorations, dry meadow gardens, and cut-flower borders.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

A tropical-looking small understory tree with luxuriant, drooping oblong leaves up to 12 inches long that turn bright butter-yellow in autumn. Strange, nodding bell-shaped maroon flowers emerge before foliage, giving rise to heavy, custard-like edible native fruits.

Growth Habit & Form: Grows 15–25 ft tall and wide; slow-growing, forming colonial thickets via creeping root runners if suckers are unmanaged.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Colonial thicket former; ideal for massing in shade matrices alongside ferns, wild ginger, and spicebush.

Recommended Garden Settings: Edible native orchards, woodland borders, shaded stream banks, and naturalized colonies.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

maintenance_guide.spring: Prune away unwanted root suckers in early spring if a single-stemmed tree form is desired. Hand-pollinate blossoms with a small brush if abundant fruit set is wanted.
maintenance_guide.summer: Requires consistent moisture during fruit swell in midsummer. Protect young trees from harsh full midday sun.
maintenance_guide.fall: Harvest ripe fruit as skin softens and releases a rich tropical mango-banana aroma in September. Rake fallen foliage to prevent fungal build-up.

advisor_description:
A delightful native woodland succulent forming creeping mats of rounded, fleshy green leaves arranged in distinctive whorls of three, covered in May and June with charming sprays of starry, 4-petaled pure white blossoms with dark purplish anthers.

Growth Habit & Form: Creeping, mat-forming succulent 3–6 inches tall spreading 12–18 inches wide, rooting readily at leaf nodes.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Shade succulent groundcover; carpets rocky shade soils alongside wild columbine and maidenhair fern.

Recommended Garden Settings: Shaded rock gardens, stone wall crevices, shaded borders, woodland paths, and shaded trough containers.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Classic woodland matrix perennial; pairs seamlessly with bluebells, woodland phlox, columbine, and sedges.

Recommended Garden Settings: Dappled shade woodland borders, shade gardens, cottage borders, and naturalized woods.

Growth Habit & Form: Clump-forming, arching perennial 12–18 inches tall and 12–15 inches wide with succulent stems.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Woodland edge companion; pairs with wild columbine, wild geranium, and carex sedges.

Recommended Garden Settings: Dappled woodland gardens, moist shady borders, rockeries, and cottage paths.

Renowned for arguably the most spectacular autumn foliage of any North American native tree—exploding in kaleidoscopic blends of fiery scarlet, tangerine, amber, and plum purple. Spring brings purplish-pink smokey panicles that hover like mist over round, blue-green leaves.

Growth Habit & Form: Slow-growing small tree reaching 20–30 ft with a rounded, open crown. Thrives in shallow, rocky limestone soils where other trees struggle.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Architectural specimen tree; exceptional focal point in drought-hardy mixed native shrub and grass plantings.

Recommended Garden Settings: Limestone glades, dry rocky slopes, sunny courtyard focal points, and low-water xeriscapes.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

advisor_description:
An architectural woodland aristocrat featuring arching, zig-zagging stems clothed in two-ranked alternate glossy green leaves, terminated in May with a feathery, fragrant plume of creamy-white starry flowers, followed by clusters of ruby-red berries in autumn.

Growth Habit & Form: Arching, elegant perennial 2–3 ft tall and 2 ft wide, forming slow-growing clumps via creeping rootstocks.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Structural shade perennial; combines exquisitely with Christmas fern, Solomon's seal, and wild hydrangea.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rich woodland shade gardens, shaded borders, north-facing slopes, and native shade matrices.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

advisor_description:
A majestic wetland iris producing elegant, sword-like blue-green leaves up to 3 ft tall and bearing magnificent, violet-blue blossoms with intricately veined yellow and white crests on the falls in May and June.

Growth Habit & Form: Upright, clumping perennial 2–3 ft tall and 2 ft wide that spreads steadily via thick underground rhizomes.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Wetland matrix structural anchor; pairs with swamp milkweed, blue pickerel, and fox sedge.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rain gardens, bioswales, retention pond margins, water garden shallows, and bog borders.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

advisor_description:
A superb, rugged evergreen native groundcover featuring lustrous, strawberry-like trifoliate foliage that forms a dense, weed-suppressing carpet, topped in April and May with cheerful clusters of 5-petaled buttercup-yellow blossoms.

Growth Habit & Form: Low, creeping mat 4–8 inches tall spreading 12–18 inches wide via shallow rhizomatous runners.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Evergreen living mulch; suppresses weeds beneath deciduous shrubs and along shaded garden borders.

Recommended Garden Settings: Shaded rock gardens, woodland borders, path edging, dry shade under trees, and erosion control slopes.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

Versatile, rugged native shrub covered in late spring with 4-inch flat-topped clusters of creamy-white blossoms, followed by glossy, coarsely toothed foliage, deep blue-black berries in late summer, and wine-red to yellow fall foliage.

Growth Habit & Form: Forms a dense, rounded, multi-stemmed upright shrub 6–10 ft tall and wide, suckering gently to form loose colonies.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Structural wildlife anchor; host plant for spring azure butterflies and preferred nesting site for catbirds and cardinals.

Recommended Garden Settings: Privacy screens, rain gardens, naturalized hedgerows, and bird sanctuary borders.

Growth Habit & Form: Upright, unbranched clump 2–3 ft tall and 1–1.5 ft wide with a fibrous, non-aggressive root crown.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Late-season bumblebee magnet; combines magnificently with cardinal flower, swamp milkweed, and carex.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rain gardens, bioswales, stream banks, moist shady borders, and wet meadow restorations.

Growth Habit & Form: Colonial, creeping perennial 12–18 inches tall, spreading via underground rhizomes into dense umbrella colonies.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Deciduous shade matrix canopy; carpets woodland floors, pairing with trilliums, bluebells, and ferns.

Recommended Garden Settings: Naturalized woodland gardens, shade borders under tall oaks, shaded slopes, and forest floor restorations.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

Growth Habit & Form: Upright, succulent clump 1.5–2 ft tall and 1.5 ft wide with fleshy, deep taproots.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Spring ephemeral matrix superstar; interplants with ferns and carex that expand to fill the space when bluebells go dormant.

Recommended Garden Settings: Moist woodland gardens, deciduous forest floors, shaded borders, and spring bulb beds.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

Growth Habit & Form: Upright, multi-stemmed clump 1–2 ft tall and 1–1.5 ft wide with a deep, drought-proof woody taproot.

Growth Habit & Form: Upright, bushy branched clump 3–5 ft tall and 2–3 ft wide with a fibrous, non-aggressive root crown.

Sociability & Matrix Role: High-value prairie structural perennial; pairs with big bluestem, switchgrass, and New England aster.

Recommended Garden Settings: Sunny perennial borders, prairie meadows, rain garden edges, and pollinator cutting gardens.

maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping or occasional division) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back previous year's dead stalks at 50°F+, leaving 12 inches of stubble for solitary bee nesting.
maintenance_guide.summer: Highly drought and heat tolerant; thrives in average to moist garden soils in full sun. Pinch in June for compact height.
maintenance_guide.fall: Sweet anise-scented cones turn dark chocolate; seeds are a top favorite of American Goldfinches.

advisor_description:
A colossal, rapid-growing canopy aristocrat with straight columnar trunk and unique 4-lobed leaves resembling tulip silhouettes. In late spring, high branches bear magnificent green and orange cup-shaped tulip flowers, turning brilliant golden-yellow in fall.

Growth Habit & Form: Soars 70–90 ft tall with a 40–50 ft spread. Fast-growing pyramidal tree in youth, rounding with age.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Grand canopy keystone for spacious sites; pairs with pawpaw, spicebush, and woodland phlox understory.

Recommended Garden Settings: Large residential estates, public parks, open lawn groves, and forest canopy restoration.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

advisor_description:
Widely regarded as the most spectacular, well-behaved native goldenrod, bearing magnificent, dense, club-like cylindrical plumes of brilliant golden-yellow florets from August to October, held above clean, smooth, reddish-tinted erect stems.

Growth Habit & Form: Stately, upright clumping perennial 2–4 ft tall and 1.5–2 ft wide with non-invasive fibrous root crowns.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Late-season pollinator keystone; non-aggressive clump former (does not run); pairs with little bluestem and asters.

Recommended Garden Settings: Formal native borders, pollinator meadows, prairie restorations, and autumn cut-flower gardens.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

advisor_description:
A late-summer prairie glade beauty producing upright, globe-shaped umbels of starry pink-lavender blossoms in August and September that stand erect on wiry stems above narrow, grass-like green foliage.

Growth Habit & Form: Clump-forming bulbous perennial 1–2 ft tall and 1 ft wide with non-invasive bulb clusters.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Late-season glade pollinator magnet; completely deer- and rabbit-proof; pairs with sideoats grama and aromatic aster.

Recommended Garden Settings: Dry sunny borders, limestone glades, rock gardens, curbside hellstrips, and pollinator meadows.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

Unique, exotic native shrub bearing intriguing strap-petaled deep maroon to burgundy blossoms in late spring that emit a intoxicating fruity fragrance reminiscent of strawberries, melons, and crushed apples. Broad lustrous leaves turn golden-yellow in fall.

Growth Habit & Form: Grows 6–9 ft tall and 6–12 ft wide with a dense, rounded, suckering multi-stemmed framework.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Fragrant focal shrub; blends seamlessly into partial shade shrub borders and woodland clearings.

Recommended Garden Settings: Sensory gardens, patio foundation perimeters, fragrant borders, and woodland edges.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

A towering, regal native perennial bearing massive, domed corymbs of vanilla-scented dusty rose to mauve-pink florets from July to September, carried in dramatic tiered whorls of lance-shaped leaves along stout, purple-speckled stems.

Growth Habit & Form: Magnificent, upright clump 4–7 ft tall and 3–4 ft wide with a massive fibrous root crown.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Premier butterfly beacon; companions include swamp milkweed, New England aster, and prairie cordgrass.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rain gardens, moist meadow borders, pond shorelines, and back-of-border architectural backdrops.

The dazzling 'Butterfly Weed' producing brilliant, flat-topped clusters of fiery orange to tangerine-yellow blossoms from June to August that glow like living embers, set against hairy, lance-shaped leaves on sturdy stems with clear (non-milky) sap.

Growth Habit & Form: Bushy, multi-stemmed clump 1.5–2.5 ft tall and 1.5–2 ft wide arising from a massive, deep woody taproot.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Crown jewel of sunny pollinator borders; premier monarch host and nectar source; pairs with little bluestem and coneflowers.

Recommended Garden Settings: Sunny perennial borders, prairie restorations, dry rocky glades, rock gardens, and curbside hellstrips.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

advisor_description:
A whimsical, moisture-loving shrub bearing spherical, 1.5-inch white flower balls bristling with protruding pistils like celestial pin-cushions or mini satellites from June to August. Attracts hordes of butterflies, followed by spherical reddish-brown seed balls.

Growth Habit & Form: Grows 6–12 ft tall and wide with an open, spreading, multi-stemmed habit. Thrives with roots submerged in water.

Sociability & Matrix Role: Wetland matrix keystone; pairs with swamp milkweed, blue flag iris, and cardinal flower in wet basins.

Recommended Garden Settings: Rain gardens, retention ponds, bioswales, shoreline margins, and wet low-lying garden beds.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

advisor_description:
The celebrated 'Aromatic Aster', forming a spectacular, dense, compact mounding dome that smothers itself in October and November with hundreds of vivid royal violet-blue daisies with golden centers. Foliage releases a delightful minty-balsam aroma when crushed.

Growth Habit & Form: Dense, rounded, multi-branched subshrub mound 1.5–2.5 ft tall and 2–3 ft wide.

Sociability & Matrix Role: The ultimate late-autumn finale; pairs with prairie dropseed, little bluestem, and showy goldenrod.

Recommended Garden Settings: Sunny borders, rock gardens, retaining wall edges, curbside hellstrips, and highway slopes.

Sources: Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder, Grow Native! (Missouri Prairie Foundation), Sow Wild Natives, City Roots Nursery, MDC.

Growth Habit & Form: Spreading groundcover 1–2 ft tall and 1.5–2 ft wide with creeping rhizomes that form a dense green mat.
